validation.result: Fresh git pull --ff-only succeeded before detailed investigation on clean isolated main. Original diverged checkout untouched.
bun install --frozen-lockfile succeeded with normal Husky; source and lockfile unchanged.
bun run test:coverage passed 534 tests, with four existing Bun-native startup tests skipped by the Node-based runner. All current coverage thresholds passed. Log /tmp/readme-frogie-unit-tests.log.
bun run build passed server and frontend compilation; existing large-bundle and Vite native config-loader compatibility warnings retained. No tracked generated differences.

Actual startServer used an owned temporary SQLite/data directory and ephemeral ports. Real Hono Google routes with mocked token/userinfo replies plus Chromium verified the same-origin localhost callback and Secure session cookie. Anonymous settings access matched the documented authentication boundary. All temporary servers/data were cleaned up; no real Google/model requests or personal data. Log /tmp/readme-frogie-auth-probe.log.

Default test:l3 was not run: it starts/reuses personal ~/.frogie and ports 7033/7034, lacks a login fixture and attempts real chat. README documents prerequisites instead of claiming this suite is isolated or passing.
GitHub metadata homepage is null; site project website is also null. frogie.dev.hexly.ai is a local development host, so only the language link appears. Actual LICENSE is MIT.
All local image/document links resolve in both languages. Bash and dotenv examples match; fenced blocks balance. No README gate, hook or 6DQ material.

Normal pre-commit passed types, lint and coverage. Fresh git pull --ff-only origin main before push succeeded with only the reviewed README commit ahead. Normal pre-push actually passed both scanners without warning-only failures. Logs /tmp/readme-frogie-commit.log and /tmp/readme-frogie-push.log.

Installed osv-scanner scanned bun.lock (557 packages) with the repository configuration and found no issues. Installed gitleaks scanned the working tree (261.48 MB) and found no leaks. Both commands exited 0; logs /tmp/readme-frogie-osv.log and /tmp/readme-frogie-gitleaks.log. This is a working-tree scan, not a claim of full-history scanning.
